title: Acute Diverticulitis — Complicated (2 cm Pericolic Abscess)
diagnosis: Acute Diverticulitis, complicated by 2 cm pericolic abscess
patient: 50M, LLQ pain, nausea, vomiting, fever 38.2, HR 115, leukocytosis
correctOrders: Physical Exam: General Appearance, Chest/Lungs, Heart/CV, Abdomen, Rectal
IV antibiotics: ciprofloxacin AND metronidazole (or ampicillin/sulbactam, etc.)

missedOrders.why: Gold standard for diverticulitis diagnosis. Identifies abscess vs uncomplicated. X-ray cannot see the 2 cm pericolic abscess. Directly drives management: <3-4 cm = medical only, >4 cm = percutaneous drainage.
Inflamed sigmoid sits on bladder → sterile pyuria. Distinguish from pyelonephritis/renal colic. Same quadrant, same presentation.
Fever + abscess → bacteremia risk. Draw before antibiotics for organism identification and sensitivity-guided therapy.
Abdominal pain + fever + leukocytosis → rule out UTI/pyelo as cause.
Bowel rest. Sigmoid generates 90 mmHg during peristalsis — highest in GI tract. Every wave drives bacteria through microperforated wall into abscess.
Long-term prevention. Larger soft stool → lower intraluminal pressure → less herniation. Current standard of care despite ongoing study questions.

wrongLocation.reason: Patient requires IV fluids and inpatient monitoring

shouldHaveAvoided.why: Contraindicated during acute diverticulitis — risk of perforation of inflamed bowel. Defer 4-6 weeks after resolution to rule out malignancy.

descent3x3.description: Pathophysiology arc: osis → itis → abscess → antibiotics → recovery

descentGaps1.description: Diagnostic orders: CT vs XR, blood cultures, UA, cipro + metronidazole mechanism

descentGaps2.description: Management: NPO, pain, inpatient transfer, fiber, colonoscopy, lifelong plan

caseSummary: The classic triad of diverticulitis is left lower quadrant pain, low-grade fever, and leukocytosis. CT with contrast is the gold standard. Findings in this case: 2 cm pericolic abscess (complicated). Abscesses <3-4 cm managed conservatively with IV antibiotics. Colonoscopy is contraindicated acutely — defer 4-6 weeks. High fiber diet for long-term prevention.
